objective: Proof and verification. (1) Plane matching systems: a plane signed system with as many lines as odd faces has as solutions the perfect matchings of lines to odd faces, and the access lemma of PLANAR-THEOREM A and C holds on it for every pinning; a plane knot space split at a point into three ports is one. (2) The interface lemma: in a splice of a knot space minus a line with a knot space split at a point, with any line removed, the solutions restricted to either piece are that piece's closure minus a line, the point-split closure, or a gadget form, each a plane matching system when the closure is plane. (3) Hence every pinning by two points of a plane piece has access. Verify on point splits of plane spaces and on Fano-plane splices; record pinnings from outside the piece.
status: Proved by HANDLE-LOCALITY-20261103-001A-P001: access is local. Plane signed systems with as many lines as odd faces have perfect matchings as solutions and the access lemma for every pinning; a plane knot space split at a point is one. In a splice, an intact side acts on the cut as the closing point or line, so the solutions restricted to a plane piece are its closure minus a line, the point split, or a gadget form, each a matching system. title: Access is local: plane pieces keep it
